title: Shaping columns
summary: Keep the columns the report needs, give each one a clear name and the right data type, and use Column quality to find the values that won’t convert. Naming what you keep is safer than naming what you drop.
objectives: Choose the columns to keep with Remove Other Columns or Choose Columns, and explain why it’s safer than Remove Columns.
Pick the right number type: Whole, Decimal, Fixed decimal or Percentage.
Find and handle errors from a type change with Column quality and Replace Errors.

p: Remove Columns names the columns you drop. Remove Other Columns names the ones you keep. When next month’s file has an extra column, only one of them keeps it out.
Select the columns to keep (Ctrl+click), then Remove Columns ▾ › Remove Other Columns.
Choose Columns lists every column with a tick box.
Either writes `Table.SelectColumns(…, {…})`.
In real life: added a “Warehouse” column in June. Ishaan’s report didn’t notice, because it names what it keeps.

p: Double-click a heading to rename it. Each rename becomes part of a Renamed Columns step. Short, plain names make every later formula and PivotTable easier to read.
Renames in a row are kept in one step.
Move columns with Transform › Move, or by dragging the heading.
Order matters to readers, not to Power Query.
In real life: asked what “Cust_Nm_1” meant. It’s “Customer” now.

p: Power Query has four number types. Whole Number for counts, Decimal Number for measurements, Fixed decimal number for money and Percentage for rates.
Fixed decimal avoids tiny rounding errors when money is added up.
Whole Number rounds 2.5 to 2: half to even.
Text like "18%" converts to 0.18 as a Percentage.
In real life: is held as 18% text in the product list. As a Percentage it becomes 0.18, ready to multiply.

p: View › Column quality shows, under each heading, how many values are valid, errors or empty. After a type change, any Error is a value that wouldn’t convert.
Click an Error cell to see why: DataFormat.Error, and the value.
Errors don’t stop the query, but they load as empty cells.
Fix the cause, or use Replace Errors or Remove Errors.
In real life: said “on request” for the new LED panel. As a number it became an Error, and Column quality showed it at once.

p: Right-click a column › Replace Errors puts a value of your choice, often null, where the errors are. Remove Errors drops the whole row. Pick what the report needs.
null is Power Query’s empty value.
Keep Errors on a copy of the query is a handy checker.
The best fix is at the source: ask for a price.
In real life: replaced the MRP error with null and asked purchasing for the price. The product stays in the list meanwhile.

lab.intro: The product list is the Table **Items** on the **Products** sheet. The query **Items** is open. Shape it for the price report.

tasks.prompt: Keep only **Item Code, Item Name, Category, MRP, Dealer Price** and **GST %**, in a way that keeps out any column added next month.
hints: Home › Remove Columns ▾ › Remove Other Columns.
Or Home › Choose Columns and tick the six.
tasks.solution:
let
    Source = Excel.CurrentWorkbook(){[Name="Items"]}[Content],
    #"Changed Type" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Source,{{"Item Code", type text}, {"Item Name", type text}, {"Category", type text}, {"HSN", Int64.Type}, {"Unit", type text}, {"Dealer Price", Int64.Type}, {"GST %", Percentage.Type}, {"Discontinued", type text}, {"Remarks", type text}, {"Updated By", type text}}),
    #"Removed Other Columns" = Table.SelectColumns(#"Changed Type",{"Item Code", "Item Name", "Category", "MRP", "Dealer Price", "GST %"})
in

quiz.q: Which step survives a new column in next month’s file?
Where do you turn on Column quality?
Replace Errors with null on MRP…
quiz.explain: Remove Errors would drop the rows.

quiz.q: Several renames in a row become…
quiz.explain: Power Query adds them to the same step.

points: Name what you **keep**: Remove Other Columns or Choose Columns write `Table.SelectColumns`.
Pick the type that fits: **Whole**, **Decimal**, **Fixed decimal** (money), **Percentage**.
**Column quality** finds errors; **Replace Errors** or **Remove Errors** handles them.
recap.cheat: Keep columns by name; types that fit (money = Fixed decimal); Column quality finds errors.
